label: D2 after a2 led rarely to S1 (a2->S1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the shown state is S1 (never on D1/GO or S2). Within that, 94% of activation mass is on a2 -> S1, i.e. the rare transition after choosing a2 (dev P 0.94, R 0.90, F1 0.92). The remaining ~6% of mass are weak activations on a1 -> S1 common D2 steps. Uses only current inputs (in_state, in_action), so it is fully observed. Magnitude is highest when the agent is in an a2-preferring regime (good = S2, previous choice a2, strong a2 policy logit): the top windows are repeated a2 -> S1 rare trials with good = S2, and restricting to good == 2 raises precision to 0.97 but costs recall. Inactive cases among a2 -> S1 are mostly ones where good = S1 or the agent had just switched to a2. Does not fire on S2 arrivals, common a2 -> S2, or any non-D2 step.

issues: Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.932, R 0.895, F1 0.913, mass recall 0.943.
'Fires only at D2 on S1' holds. phase==GO, phase==D1 and D2&S2 all cover 0 of the active steps in every activation quartile. D2&S1 covers all of them.
The misses (6281 steps, 5.7% of mass) are weak firing on common a1->S1 D2 steps, as claimed. They cover only 0.7% of the top activation quartile.

The false positives (3874) are a2->S1 steps where good=S1 or the agent had just switched to a2, which is what the explanation says. Excluding (good==1 & previous action==1) gives a test F1 of 0.912, so it adds nothing. Requiring (good==2 | previous action==2) gives F1 0.884. So no systematic gap is left that a better predicate fixes.
Small caveat: a stricter reading of the unit is 'D2 with S1 shown, strongest after a2'. The label stresses the rare transition, which matches about 94% of the mass, so this is acceptable.
